messages:
maria_g: Quick sync — planning to enable the cache+microbatching flag for a small slice tomorrow AM. want eyes on the guardrails before i flip it.
prashant: Thanks. which flag key and where will it be toggled (ld/flagservice)?
sam_dev: flag = `enable_batch_cache_v3` in our internal FF service. will target traffic slices by customer_tier and region.
elaine: Can we start with 1% noisy customers + internal-only traffic? also include a zero-downtime fallback to single-token mode.
maria_g: Yup — plan: 1) 1% prod global customers 2) + 100% staging + 100% canary agents 3) expand to 5% after 30m if metrics OK. fallback route set to `cache_disabled` if p99 > baseline * 1.25 or error_rate > 0.5%.
raj: What are the exact dashboards/metrics we need to watch? I can be on-watch during the flip.
prashant: Primary: p50/p95/p99 latency for generate endpoints, request_error_rate, token_cost_per_request, evictions/miss_rate from KV cache. Secondary: infra GPU utilization and queue depth.
sam_dev: Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/infn/cache-batch-v3 (panel: latency-by-audience, cache-hit-ratio, token-cost). set alert thresholds before flip.
elaine: I'll create a temporary PagerDuty escalation for the next 2 hours of the canary window. pls list oncall names.
raj: I'll be the primary monitor, elaine backup. @oncall-bot please create escalation `cache-batch-v3-canary` for 2h.
oncall-bot: created escalation policy `cache-batch-v3-canary` -> primary: raj, secondary: elaine, timeout: 20m.
maria_g: Rollout pre-checklist: 1) health endpoints ok 2) canary env ran for 24h 3) loadtest scripts exercised 4) rollback playbook staged. all done?
prashant: health ok, canary ran 36h, loadtests passed at target qps, but we saw a small spike in evictions with seq>1024 — we should cap max_seq in config to 1024 for the canary.
sam_dev: config snippet i'll use: ```yaml
feature: enable_batch_cache_v3
canary: true
audience: ["internal", "1pct_public"]
max_sequence: 1024
fallback: cache_disabled
metrics_thresholds:
  p99_latency_ms: 1200
  error_rate_pct: 0.5
```
maria_g: Good. rollback procedure: flip FF -> route 100% to `cache_disabled` -> monitor for 10m -> if okay, revert infra changes. Who runs the flip?
raj: I'll run the toggle and stay on call for 1h. please DM me right before so i can quiet notifications.
prashant: Add a canary traffic slicer: `customer_tags` with seed-based hashing so it's stable across restarts. also enable request-level logging for a subset (0.1%) to capture KV miss traces.
elaine: Can we have an automatic rollback script if token_cost jumps > 15% or p99 > threshold? we can wire a small lambda that calls the FF API.
sam_dev: yep we've got a script. example: ```bash
# toggle off
curl -X POST https://flags.redwood/api/v1/toggle \n -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN' \n -d '{"flag":"enable_batch_cache_v3","state":"off","note":"auto-rollback - cost spike"}'\n```
maria_g: Cool. schedule: 09:00 UTC tomorrow cut, 1% baseline -> wait 30m -> check metrics -> expand to 5% for 60m -> expand to 20% if stable. full rollout only after SRE + infra + product thumbs-up.
raj: I'll post results to this thread and tag #eng-oncall. if anything odd i'll trigger the escalation.
prashant: One more ask: mark the canary hosts with `cachebatch-v3` tag so logs/metrics are filtered.
elaine: Done. also added dashboard annotations for the start/stop times.
maria_g: thanks team. flip window confirmed 09:00 UTC. i'll ping 08:50 to gather crew.
raj: on it.
prashant: lgtm.
sam_dev: lgtm :thumbsup:
elaine: :thumbsup:
